questions.question: If the rear of your vehicle is skidding to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Do not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left.
Turn your steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: When you skid on a wet or icy road, remove your foot from the accelerator and brakes. Turn your steering wheel in the direction the rear is skidding. If you have anti-lock brakes, press the brakes firmly and steer straight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are approaching a school or school crosswalk.
Slow down, drive with caution, and watch for children.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers near schools to slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.

questions.question: If you see flooded water ahead on the road, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard.
Do not drive through. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded roads. Water may hide danger even if it looks shallow. Turn around and use a different route.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield sign ahead.
Side road entering from left.
Stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a yield sign is coming. Slow down when you see it.

questions.question: You park downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead.
Right, toward the side of the road.
Left, toward the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road.
questions.explanation: When parked downhill on a road without a curb, turn wheels right toward the edge so the car rolls away from traffic if brakes fail. When parked uphill on a road without a curb, turn wheels left toward the center. When parked uphill on a road with a curb, turn wheels left so the car rolls into the curb.

questions.question: Which statement is true about medicines and driving?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines are safe for driving if you use the correct dose.
It is safe to take any medicine if a doctor prescribes it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medicines—prescription or over-the-counter—can affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy. Know how your medicine affects your ability to drive.

questions.question: When is it legal to drive in a bicycle lane?

options.text: When the lane is empty and you need the space.
When passing another vehicle.
When parking (where allowed), entering or leaving the road, or turning (within 200 feet of an intersection).

questions.correctAnswerText: When parking (where allowed), entering or leaving the road, or turning (within 200 feet of an intersection).
questions.explanation: You can only drive in a bicycle lane when parking where permitted, entering or leaving the road, or turning within 200 feet of an intersection.

questions.question: When you see someone crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until they are far away from your vehicle.
Honk your horn and continue.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until they are far away from your vehicle.
questions.explanation: When a blind person using a white cane or guide dog crosses in front of you, stop completely until they are well away from your path. Always give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: If your car's suspension is bad, what can it cause?

options.text: Vehicle control problems.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicle control problems.
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and gives a smooth ride. If your car bounces a lot after bumps or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: What can happen if you abandon an animal on the highway?

options.text: Jail time.
A point against your license.
No legal consequences.

questions.correctAnswerText: Jail time.
questions.explanation: Dumping or abandoning an animal on the highway is illegal. You can face up to six months in jail, a fine of up to $1,000, or both.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must yield to:

options.text: Any driver on your left.
Any driver who arrived before you.
Any driver across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any driver who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: Vehicles at a four-way stop go through in the order they arrived. If multiple vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
Warning of danger ahead.
Signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning of danger ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow diamond-shaped signs warn of possible danger. Orange diamond-shaped signs warn of dangers in or near work areas.

questions.question: To enter a gap in traffic on the highway, you should:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and make other vehicles move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, check to the side and behind your vehicle. Make sure no cars are in your way.

questions.question: What is the difference between a red arrow and a solid red light?

options.text: Red arrows only stop turning traffic.
Red arrows only protect turn lanes.
You cannot turn on a red arrow, even if you stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn on a red arrow, even if you stop first.
questions.explanation: You may turn right at a solid red light after stopping. You can never turn left or right at a red arrow, even if you stop first.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid yellow line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, drivers on the broken line side can pass. Drivers on the solid line side cannot pass.

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street. You can only turn left onto another one-way street if:

options.text: You drive faster before turning.
Traffic moves to the right.
Traffic moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the left if there is no sign blocking the turn. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: When a bicyclist is turning left:

options.text: They can use the left lane.
They can cut across all lanes.
They must wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride with traffic on the road. You should expect to see a bicyclist in the left lane when they are turning left.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Stay one car length behind the car in front.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Scan ahead to watch for dangers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan ahead to watch for dangers.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking far ahead for possible hazards. Do not stare only at the road in front of your car. Look ahead and watch the vehicles around you.

questions.question: When driving on a street with multiple lanes and two-way traffic:

options.text: Drive next to other vehicles so they can see you.
Drive ahead of or behind other vehicles.
It is safest to drive in the lane closest to the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive ahead of or behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Driving next to another vehicle is dangerous. The other driver may drift into your lane or change lanes without looking. Stay ahead of or behind other vehicles to avoid crashes.

questions.question: Which statement is true about alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are below the legal alcohol limit, your driving is not impaired.
Alcohol harms your judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol harms your judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. Good judgment helps you react to things you see while driving. Even below the legal limit, any alcohol can make you a less safe driver.

questions.question: To see traffic behind you:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror often to know where vehicles are behind you.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating high-fat foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body.

questions.question: What is an important step when turning?

options.text: Check traffic in all directions.
Drive faster.
Always move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: When turning, look behind you and to both sides of your vehicle. Make sure it is safe before turning. Slow down to complete the turn safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The vehicle has the right-of-way.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Road work ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles like farm tractors and road maintenance trucks display an orange and red triangle on the back.

questions.question: A white painted curb means:

options.text: Loading zone for freight or passengers.
Loading zone for passengers or mail only.
Loading zone for freight only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loading zone for passengers or mail only.
questions.explanation: At a white curb, you can stop only to pick up or drop off passengers or mail.

questions.question: Two sets of solid double yellow lines that are two or more feet apart:

options.text: Can be crossed to enter or exit a driveway.
Cannot be crossed for any reason.
Should be treated as a separate traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot be crossed for any reason.
questions.explanation: Two sets of solid double yellow lines spaced two or more feet apart are a barrier. Do not drive on or cross this barrier, except at marked openings.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Right-of-way rules tell you who should go first, but do not assume you have the right-of-way. Always be ready to yield if it prevents a crash.

questions.question: A blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Does not affect your driving.
Does not put other drivers at risk.
Doubles your chance of a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doubles your chance of a crash.
questions.explanation: Every 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol nearly doubles your risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: A flashing red light means:

options.text: Slow down before entering.
Stop before entering.
Stop and wait for green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. After stopping, go when it is safe. Follow all right-of-way rules.

questions.question: Which vehicle must always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: Tanker trucks with hazardous materials labels.
Motor homes or trucks towing a boat trailer.
Any vehicle with three or more axles weighing over 4,000 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tanker trucks with hazardous materials labels.
questions.explanation: Trucks carrying hazardous materials must stop before crossing railroad tracks.
